nucleus.thesis: Decouple open-source model distribution from deployment capability: release weights transparently to prevent monopoly, gate large-scale compute access to distribute stewardship responsibility.

claims.text: Safety externalities are real and distributed; closed systems prevent neither misuse nor reverse-engineering, only accountability. Governance architecture—not access control—is the actual crux.

Staged release by capability level—research community first, broader access after validation—prevents both monopoly lock-in and reckless proliferation without assuming access equals consequence-free deployment.

Open weights + compute verification gates: transparency prevents gatekeeping power concentration; deployment friction requires distributed stewardship without suppressing safety-infrastructure innovation.

License restrictions should target specific dual-use harms (biosynthesis, surveillance scale) rather than blanket models. Dual-use risk varies by capability; graduated friction matches actual vectors.
Federated independent review bodies distribute power across multiple institutions. Neither single gatekeeper nor ungoverned proliferation—governance distributes as innovatively as capability.

shell.topic: Should open-source AI models be freely distributed?
